location.description: Used to find the parent resource to bind the IAM policy to. If not specified, the value will be parsed from the identifier of the parent resource. If no location is provided in the parent identifier and no location is specified, it is taken from the provider configuration.
location.rationale: Defines the geographical scope of IAM permissions for restore operations. Must align with approved regions for compliance and proper access control.

name.rationale: Resource identifier for IAM binding. No direct security impact but essential for proper IAM policy attachment to restore plans.

project.description: If it is not provided, the project will be parsed from the identifier of the parent resource. If no project is provided in the parent identifier and no project is specified, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Defines the project scope for IAM permissions on restore operations. Critical for ensuring access controls are applied within the correct organizational boundary.

member/members.description: Each entry can have one of the following values: * **allUsers**: A special identifier that represents anyone who is on the internet; with or without a Google account. * **allAuthenticatedUsers**: A special identifier that represents anyone who is authenticated with a Google account or a service account. * **user:{emailid}**: An email address that represents a specific Google account. For example, alice@gmail.com or joe@example.com. * **serviceAccount:{emailid}**: An email address that represents a service account. For example, my-other-app@appspot.gserviceaccount.com. * **group:{emailid}**: An email address that represents a Google group. For example, admins@example.com. * **domain:{domain}**: A G Suite domain (primary, instead of alias) name that represents all the users of that domain. For example, google.com or example.com. * **projectOwner:projectid**: Owners of the given project. For example, "projectOwner:my-example-project" * **projectEditor:projectid**: Editors of the given project. For example, "projectEditor:my-example-project" * **projectViewer:projectid**: Viewers of the given project. For example, "projectViewer:my-example-project"
member/members.rationale: CRITICAL: Defines who has access to restore plans and can perform restore operations. Public principals (allUsers, allAuthenticatedUsers) create massive security risks by allowing anyone to restore backup data potentially to unauthorized locations. Restore permissions are extremely sensitive as they control access to backup data and disaster recovery capabilities.

role.description: `google_gke_backup_restore_plan_iam_binding` can be used per role. Note that custom roles must be of the format `[projects|organizations]/{parent-name}/roles/{role-name}`.
role.rationale: Defines the level of access granted to restore resources. Must follow principle of least privilege. Restore permissions should be highly restricted as they provide access to potentially sensitive backup data.

policy_data.rationale: Alternative method for defining IAM policies. Must ensure no public principals are included and that restore permissions are appropriately restricted.
policy_data.compliant: Policy without public principals and with least privilege access
policy_data.non-compliant: Policy containing allUsers, allAuthenticatedUsers, or overly broad permissions
